summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, and chronic bronchitis was admitted due to increased green sputum production, difficulty clearing tracheal secretions, and worsening shortness of breath, similar to a recent hospitalization. She had been on oral cefuroxime and fluconazole but was not improving. IV ceftriaxone was started, and she showed clinical improvement overnight. A sputum culture showed only commensal flora, and no fungal growth was detected. The pulmonary team recommended completing a 10-day course of IV ceftriaxone and oral fluconazole, along with a 4-day course of azithromycin. She was discharged home with home IV antibiotic therapy, clear instructions, and a plan for follow-up with her pulmonologist.
problems: Obstructive chronic bronchitis with acute bronchitis
